newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint ends little changed vs dlr, c.bank basket.
newsitem.headline: Forint ends little changed vs dlr, c.bank basket.

text.p: The Hungarian forint closed virtually steady on Friday, a little firmer against the dollar and a shade weaker versus the central bank's currency basket in routine business, dealers said.

The forint finished at 182.35/40 to the U.S. unit, compared to 182.42/47 at the opening, and by the close had widened the gap that separates it from the central bank's resistance level to 30 pips from 20 to 25 pips in the morning.
Dealers predicted the forint would reduce the gap to around 15 to 20 pips next week, unless more negative developments on the Czech market trigger new fears.
"We'll open with a gap next week and unless anything special happens on the Czech markets we'll go back to 15 to 20 pips," said Robert Szucs of Inter-Europa Bank.
Traders added, however, that some more time was needed for the forint to return to the bid from where it distanced itself amid recent downward pressure on the Czech crown.
"Later we expect to approach the central bank's bid but this is unlikely to happen next week," the dealer added.
The forint floats within the central bank's 4.5 percent wide intervention range, against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
